title: Machine learning guides direct synthesis of higher-silica faujasite
summary: Machine-learning models learned relationships between crystallization composition/conditions and zeolite characteristics from prior synthesis records, guiding human selection of conditions for faujasite synthesis. The team reports directly synthesized, unseeded, organic-structure-directing-agent-free FAU with Si/Al 3.5, compared with the prior reported maximum 2.8. Following ion exchange, laboratory tests report improved propane cracking and dehydrogenation rates per proton site relative to the lower-silica comparator. The FAU framework was already known; this result concerns composition and route, not a new framework or industrial performance.
ai_technology: Geometric harmonics, neural networks and Gaussian-process regression
organization: University of Minnesota; Dalian University of Technology; Johns Hopkins University; Argonne National Laboratory; California Institute of Technology; Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory

source_review.scope: Primary Caltech institutional record and deposited published article/supplement; date, affiliations, methods and abstract/results.

evidence.tested: Researchers synthesized and characterized FAU and tested acid catalysts in propane cracking/dehydrogenation under laboratory conditions.
evidence.unknown: Known framework; activity comparison is assay-specific and does not establish industrial gains.
evidence.ai_role: Models trained on prior synthesis records identified composition/condition settings that guided direct high-silica FAU synthesis.
